systemStatus.headline: FRI SEP 11 7:45 AM PT REFRESH. BROWSER ACCESS WORKED THIS RUN -- GOOGLE ADS AND YELP ADS WERE BOTH CAPTURED LIVE, which clears the biggest coverage gap of the last two days. ONE THING DOMINATES TODAY AND IT IS NOT THE KITCHEN. (1) GOOGLE ADS IS BLEEDING MONEY AND GETTING WORSE EVERY DAY. Sep 10 spent $76.07 against a $40.00 daily account budget -- 90% over, after 52% over the day before. Average cost-per-click has gone $1.17 (Sep 8) to $3.04 (Sep 9) to $4.00 (Sep 10), nearly quadrupling in three days, while the account bought 19 clicks and recorded zero conversions. Brewhouse Lunch alone took $50.00 on a $25.00/day budget. Both live campaigns still read 'All ads limited by policy' and that limitation is now almost certainly the cause rather than background noise. TWO DAYS AT ROUGHLY 1.7X THE CAP WILL EMPTY THE MONTHLY BUDGET EARLY. Either pause the two Search campaigns today or take the policy manager pass that has now been flagged for three runs. For scale: Yelp delivered 102 leads over 30 days at $3.76 each; Google spent $76 in a day for 19 clicks. (2) YESTERDAY'S NO-COOK ALARM IS RESOLVED. Isael Salvador Narciso is back on today's roster as Cook. It is still worth thirty seconds in Sling to confirm Thursday genuinely ran without a scheduled cook rather than the digest failing to print the role. (3) TODAY IS SCHEDULED 65% HEAVIER THAN YESTERDAY. 12 employees, 14 shifts, 63.75 hours against Thursday's 38.75 -- the biggest day since the Aug 22 record Saturday. Thursday produced 30.8% labor on $4,385 of net; to hold 30% today net would need to reach roughly $7,200. Friday usually delivers, but this is the number to watch mid-shift. (4) YELP'S AUDIENCE SIZE IS STILL 'LIMITED' -- second run, and now confirmed on a clean render rather than inferred. Yelp's own warning is that control features raise cost-per-click, and CPC did rise from $1.20 to $1.30 while impressions, page visits and leads all slipped slightly. The 12 manual keywords and 5-mile radius are the likely constraints. THE GOOD NEWS: Thursday was the best sales day of the week -- net $4,385.27, +10.2% on Wednesday, on 131 orders and 177 guests. Payroll is settled and employees are paid today. WATCH ITEMS FROM THURSDAY'S CLOSEOUT: 39 void items, far above the 3-4 running all week, plus one order left open at close and Harmony Willson auto-clocked out -- the day did not close cleanly. COVERAGE GAPS THIS RUN: the Toast single-location full-detail email for Thu Sep 10 had not arrived by 14:45Z, so sales figures are group-level headline totals only and the same-day-last-week, four-week, revenue-centre and sales-category breakdowns are empty until the next refresh. yesterday.note: LIVE read, date range Yesterday (Sep 10, 2026). SEP 9 WAS THE WORST DAY ON RECORD AND SEP 10 IS WORSE. Spend $76.07 is up another $15.24 (+25%) on top of Sep 9's $60.83, and average CPC rose again to $4.00 from $3.04 -- that is a third consecutive daily increase and more than triple the $1.17 CPC of Sep 8. Volume did not follow the money: 744 impressions (+62) and 19 clicks (-1). Two days ago this account bought a click for roughly a dollar; yesterday it paid four. SPEND BREACHED THE ACCOUNT BUDGET FOR THE SECOND DAY RUNNING AND BY A WIDER MARGIN. The account daily budget is $40.00; Sep 10 spent $76.07 -- 90% over, against 52% over on Sep 9. Brewhouse Lunch took $50.00 on a $25.00/day budget (exactly 2x) for 518 impressions and 10 clicks at a $5.00 CPC. Brewhouse Dinner took $26.07 on $15.00/day for 226 impressions and 9 clicks at a $2.90 CPC and a 3.98% CTR -- the healthier of the two. Two days at roughly 1.7x the daily cap will empty a monthly budget well before month end. CONVERSIONS READ 0.00 and are still flagged as calculating; an in-product banner separately credits Brewhouse Dinner with a 200% week-on-week increase in clicks. Neither figure is reliable at this reporting lag. THE STRUCTURAL FLAG IS UNCHANGED AND THIS IS NOW ITS THIRD RUN AS PRIME SUSPECT: both live Search campaigns read 'Eligible (Limited) -- All ads limited by policy'. A policy-limited account competing for a shrinking slice of inventory is exactly what a CPC that quadruples in three days looks like. The policy manager pass is overdue. Account budget $40.00/day; 2 live campaigns, 4 paused, 2 drafts in progress.

billingPeriod.note: LIVE. $142.81 across the first 10 days of the September billing period = $14.28/day against a $13/day average budget, about 10% over. The trend reversed this run: the per-day average had fallen from $15.91 (Sep 5 read) to $14.33 (Sep 8) to $13.37 (Sep 8 billing read), and has now ticked back up. Sep 9 and Sep 10 together spent $35.88, roughly $17.94/day -- well above the $13 target. Delivery is clearly not stalled any more; if anything Yelp is now spending ahead of budget while the estimated audience size still reads Limited.

yelpAds.audienceSizeNote: STILL LIMITED -- SECOND CONSECUTIVE RUN, AND NOW CONFIRMED RATHER THAN INFERRED. The Ad settings panel rendered completely this run and Estimated audience size reads 'Limited' with Yelp's own explanation: 'Control features can limit how often your ad shows and lead to a higher cost-per-click.' The likely controls are the 12 manual keywords and the 5-mile radius. This is the single most actionable Yelp item and it has now persisted for two days. Widening the radius or letting Yelp select keywords would move it back toward Ideal. Note the cost-per-click did rise this run, from $1.20 to $1.30, exactly as the warning predicts -- though at $1.30 Yelp is still buying clicks at roughly a third of what Google Ads paid yesterday ($4.00).

yelpAds.bonusBudgetNote: CONFIRMED ABSENT, AND THIS TIME ON A CLEAN READ. The Ad settings 'All settings' panel rendered completely this run -- keywords, budget, location, design, audience size and ad preview all present -- and there is no bonus-budget line anywhere on it. Previous runs could not distinguish 'absent' from 'failed to render'. This run can: there is no active bonus budget on this account.
yelpAds.yelpListingNote: Yelp ad preview shows The Brewhouse at 775 Yelp reviews, American/Seafood/Brewpubs, 229 W Montecito St, $$, 'Locally owned & operated, Established in 1998'.
yelpAds.note: PERFORMANCE MOVED SLIGHTLY THE WRONG WAY ON EVERY HEADLINE. Versus the Sep 9 read: ad impressions 28.9k (was 29.7k), page visits from ads 362 (was 383), leads from ads 102 (was 105), cost-per-click $1.30 (was $1.20), cost-per-lead $3.76 (was $3.34). The share figures slipped too -- ads now drive 51% of page visits, down from 54%. None of these moves is large on its own and 30-day windows roll off good days, but the direction is consistent and it matches the Limited audience-size warning. CONTEXT WORTH KEEPING IN VIEW: Yelp delivered 102 leads in 30 days at $3.76 each. Google Ads spent $76.07 in a single day for 19 clicks and zero recorded conversions. Whatever is wrong with the Google account, Yelp remains the efficient channel by a wide margin.
